text: {"lessons":["I sold Stock D, B, and E while each was showing a gain, then later bought B and E back at higher prices; I should avoid trimming winners automatically and consider the cost of being out of a position.","Repeatedly buying Stock E at higher prices is not a reason by itself to buy more; each trade should follow a clear view of its prospects, valuation, and role in my overall portfolio.","My account value rose overall despite some monthly dips, and I made several no-trade months; I should keep a deliberate long-term plan and trade only when that plan or the portfolio's balance calls for it."]}
